question.problem:
$$ {x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}0 & 5 \\ 5 & 0\end{aligned}]x+[\begin{aligned}{e}^{5t} \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,x(1)=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] $$ Write down the expression that gives the solution of the initial value problem above. *Hint: ${e}^{At}=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cosh}⁡(5t) & \operatorname{sinh}⁡(5t) \\ \operatorname{sinh}⁡(5t) & \operatorname{cosh}⁡(5t)\end{aligned}],$ where $A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 5 \\ 5 & 0\end{aligned}].$*
$x(t)=\,\,$ $2\operatorname{cosh}⁡(5(t-1))+\operatorname{sinh}⁡(5(t-1))$ $\,\,+{\int }_{1}^{t}\,\,$ {{field-1}} $\,\,\text{d}s$
{{field-2}} ${e}^{5s}\operatorname{sinh}⁡(5(t-s))$
question.worked_solution:
Given the system ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)+g(t),$ where $A$ is a constant square matrix, the solution of the initial value problem can be written as the sum of the homogeneous part and a particular solution:

$$
x(t)={{{e}^{A(t-{t}_{0})}\,x({t}_{0})}_{⏟}}_{\text{homogeneous part}}+{{{\int }_{{t}_{0}}^{t}{e}^{A(t-s)}g(s)\,\text{d}s}_{⏟}}_{\text{particular solution}},
$$

where $x({t}_{0})$ is the initial condition vector. 

Let's evaluate each part separately:

- First, we find the homogeneous part. We are given that ${e}^{At}=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cosh}⁡(5t) & \operatorname{sinh}⁡(5t) \\ \operatorname{sinh}⁡(5t) & \operatorname{cosh}⁡(5t)\end{aligned}].$ So,

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{A(t-1)}\,x(1) & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cosh}⁡(5(t-1)) & \operatorname{sinh}⁡(5(t-1)) \\ \operatorname{sinh}⁡(5(t-1)) & \operatorname{cosh}⁡(5(t-1))\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{cosh}⁡(5(t-1))+\operatorname{sinh}⁡(5(t-1)) \\ 2\operatorname{sinh}⁡(5(t-1))+\operatorname{cosh}⁡(5(t-1))\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

- Next, we find the particular solution. Notice that 

$$
{e}^{A(t-s)}=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cosh}⁡(5(t-s)) & \operatorname{sinh}⁡(5(t-s)) \\ \operatorname{sinh}⁡(5(t-s)) & \operatorname{cosh}⁡(5(t-s))\end{aligned}].
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{A(t-s)}g(s) & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cosh}⁡(5(t-s)) & \operatorname{sinh}⁡(5(t-s)) \\ \operatorname{sinh}⁡(5(t-s)) & \operatorname{cosh}⁡(5(t-s))\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{e}^{5s} \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{5s}\operatorname{cosh}⁡(5(t-s)) \\ {e}^{5s}\operatorname{sinh}⁡(5(t-s))\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =[\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{cosh}⁡(5(t-1))+\operatorname{sinh}⁡(5(t-1)) \\ 2\operatorname{sinh}⁡(5(t-1))+\operatorname{cosh}⁡(5(t-1))\end{aligned}]+{\int }_{1}^{t}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{5s}\operatorname{cosh}⁡(5(t-s)) \\ {e}^{5s}\operatorname{sinh}⁡(5(t-s))\end{aligned}]\text{d}s.\end{aligned}
$$
